sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 lies in the north-east of the 1929 Berlin atlas, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left. It is mostly open land. Jefferson Avenue runs along the top and Norman Avenue along the left edge; Jackson Avenue crosses the sheet diagonally from the lower left to the right, and White Horse Pike closes the bottom. At the upper right Jefferson Avenue is lettered again on two short streets running down the page, one north of Jackson Avenue and one south of it. Block 51, between Jefferson, Norman and Jackson Avenues, is divided into long narrow lots with a row of frame dwellings and their outbuildings (autos, coops and a shed) along Jefferson Avenue, and a few more houses scattered along Jackson Avenue. A building marked auto repairing stands in the middle of the top row. The large block 50 south of Jackson Avenue is nearly empty; it holds a few houses along Jefferson Avenue at the right edge, a cellar-and-brick auto repair building, a vacant store and a bake oven near the lower right, and the building marked State Police beside the pike. A narrow strip of block 49 along the bottom edge, south of White Horse Pike, shows a gasoline station and a few dwellings with distances to frame barns. A compass rose with a north arrow stands at the upper right, with the Berlin, N.J. date stamp, and a blue patch at the left edge marks a water body belonging to the neighbouring sheet. Six-inch water pipes are shown in Jefferson Avenue, Jackson Avenue and the pike, with a four-inch pipe in the pike.
notes: Norman Avenue is Hamilton Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Jackson Avenue is Jackson Road in OpenStreetMap.
The two short streets lettered Jefferson Avenue at the right edge lie on modern Marshall Avenue.
The cross-reference numbers 3 and 5 in the margins point to the neighbouring sheets.

50 ft, one part (rotation about -42). Jefferson Av, Norman Av (Hamilton Av today), Jackson Av (Jackson Road), White Horse Pike; the short streets lettered Jefferson Av at the right edge lie on modern Marshall Avenue. Mostly open land; 5 points, Jefferson / Marshall dropped by the second pass (7 m).

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 shows the eastern edge of Berlin on both sides of the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad (Pennsylvania Railroad), drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left. North of the railroad the part runs from Central Avenue (Oak) at the top down to Atlantic Avenue beside the tracks, between Chestnut Avenue on the left and Cushman Avenue on the right; McClellan Avenue (Guest) and Hardie Avenue (Astor) run down to the railroad and Sumner crosses between them. Blocks 59, 60, 232 and 233 hold frame dwellings on long lots with auto houses, coops and storage sheds, and a small ice cream cone manufactory on McClellan Avenue. In the lower right corner of the northern half, outlined by a heavy line, stands the Onlibest Hosiery Mills, a one-storey building of cement floor and steel frame with automatic sprinklers, a watchman and approved clock, hot air heat and electric light. South of the railroad, Washington Avenue comes up from Jefferson Avenue at the bottom of the sheet and forks towards the crossings; the land east of it is the yard of the Robinson Lumber Co. (lumber and mill-work), with lumber piles along the siding, a long ware house, lumber sheds, a ware house and woodworking shop with a dust blower system, an office and stores. A siding curves off the main line into the lumber yard. The Berlin borough and township line is marked at the upper left corner. Six-inch water pipes are shown in Chestnut, McClellan, Atlantic, Washington and Jefferson Avenues, with fire hydrants at the corners. Large parts of blocks 62 and 29 are open land.
notes: Old names are printed in brackets: Central Av. (Oak), McClellan Av. (Guest), Hardie Av. (Astor).
Chestnut Avenue is Washington Avenue in OpenStreetMap; the drawn Washington Avenue south of the railroad and its right-hand fork are Washington Avenue and McClellan Avenue today.
Central Avenue is followed by NJ 73 today.
Atlantic Avenue beside the railroad is North Atlantic Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Cushman Avenue at the right edge lies on the line of modern Birch Avenue; modern Cushman Avenue is further east.
Onlibest Hosiery Mills and Robinson Lumber Co.

50 ft, one part, north to upper left (rotation about -44). Central Av (Oak, NJ 73 today), Chestnut Av (Washington Av today), McClellan Av (Guest), Hardie Av (Astor), Sumner, Atlantic Av (North Atlantic Av), Cushman Av (on modern Birch Av line), Washington Av, Jefferson Av; railroad; Onlibest Hosiery Mills (heavy outline, not an inset), Robinson Lumber Co.

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4 covers the centre of Berlin around the junction of White Horse Pike with Taunton Avenue, Gardens Avenue and Washington Avenue, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right. The Pike runs down the right side of the sheet and forks below Gardens Avenue, one branch continuing as Main and New Freedom Road towards the lower left while the Pike itself bears right to the lower edge. Taunton Avenue crosses the top of the sheet and leaves at the right; Gardens Avenue crosses the middle with a jog at Thomas Avenue, and Leroy Avenue runs along the bottom. At the Pike and Taunton Avenue stand the Breeze Publishing Co. (steam heat, power and lights, printing, letters and pulls), the post office and a frame store block with a bake house. Below Taunton Avenue, block 23 holds the Fire Department, a bakery with oven, a row of stores with offices, the Berlin Hotel, and a large garage of cement floor with a capacity of cars, with sheds and dwellings behind. West of Thomas Avenue are rows of narrow lots with a scatter of frame dwellings on blocks 45 and 231, the latter a large block of open land holding the compass rose. South of Gardens Avenue, block 44 holds wagon houses, dwellings and barns on deep lots, and block 49 at the lower right holds a large private bus garage of cement floor, heated by steam. Six-inch water pipes run in most streets, with hydrants at the corners; a ten-inch main lies in the Pike.
notes: Main is Tansboro Road in OpenStreetMap, which also meets the pike at the fork.
The street lettered Thomas Avenue is the southern part of Central Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Jackson Avenue at the right edge is Jackson Road in OpenStreetMap.
Taunton Avenue west of Central Avenue is West Taunton Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Gardens Avenue jogs about 45 m at Central Avenue; both junctions are drawn and both are in OpenStreetMap.

50 ft, one part (rotation about +28). Taunton Av, Gardens Av (jogs at Thomas Av), Thomas Av (Central Av today), Central Av, Leroy Av, Main (Tansboro Road), New Freedom Rd, Washington Av, Jackson Av, fork of the White Horse Pike. Mask notched at the top right (cartouche over block 19, drawn on sheet 8).

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5 covers a residential section of Berlin south of the business district, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left of the page. The part is bounded by Jefferson Avenue along the top, Taunton Avenue on the left, Norman Avenue on the right and the White Horse Pike along the bottom; Washington Avenue runs down the middle of the sheet and Jackson Avenue crosses the lower part diagonally to meet the pike, cutting off a triangular block (26) between the two. Haines Avenue enters from the left and ends at Taunton Avenue. Blocks 24 and 27 are divided into deep house lots with frame dwellings, auto houses, sheds, storage buildings, a coop, a poultry house and a wind mill tower. Two brick-veneered or tile dwellings stand on the Washington Avenue side of block 27. At the corner of Taunton Avenue and the pike stands the Berlin National Bank, and on the large lot 50 at the lower right is the Schultz Management bus garage, a long concrete-block building of steel frame with a cement floor. Six-inch water pipes are drawn in Jefferson Avenue, Taunton Avenue, Washington Avenue, Jackson Avenue and the pike, with a four-inch pipe along the pike as well, and fire hydrants at several corners. The left margin repeats a strip of the neighbouring sheets 8 and 4 with a few buildings, and the margins name sheets 6, 3 and 2 across the boundary streets. House numbers on the lots run along each frontage, and the White Horse Pike numbers run in the 800s.
notes: Norman Avenue is Hamilton Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Jackson Avenue is Jackson Road in OpenStreetMap.
Berlin National Bank at Taunton Avenue and the White Horse Pike.
Schultz Management bus garage on lot 50 at Norman Avenue and the White Horse Pike.

50 ft, one part, pilot sheet (rotation about -42). Jefferson Av, Taunton Av, Haines Av, Washington Av, Norman Av (Hamilton Av today), Jackson Av (Jackson Road), White Horse Pike; Berlin National Bank, Schultz bus garage.

sheet-6.description: Sheet 6 shows the northern part of central Berlin on both sides of the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad (Pennsylvania Railroad), drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left. The part is bounded by Central Avenue (Oak), which carries the Berlin borough and township line, along the top and Jefferson Avenue at the bottom right. Oak Avenue, Taunton Avenue and Chestnut Avenue run down from Central Avenue to the railroad; only Taunton Avenue continues south across the tracks to Jefferson Avenue. North of the railroad the blocks (53, 230 and 59) are largely open, with a few frame dwellings and auto houses, mostly along Chestnut Avenue. Railroad Place, a lane along the tracks, leads to the passenger station with its platform and a small waiting room at the right. South of the tracks lie the Skillman-Thomas coal yard with concrete bins and an office, a concrete block manufactory in a concrete-block building, and a storage building for broom corn with fire extinguishers, pails and barrels; blocks 32 and 29 hold a few dwellings and auto houses, one of them of concrete block. A siding runs along the south side of the main line. Six-inch water pipes are shown in Central, Oak, Taunton, Chestnut and Jefferson Avenues, with fire hydrants. The lower left of the sheet, marked as sheet 8, and the margins for sheets 3 and 5 are left blank or only outlined.
notes: The railroad is lettered W. J. & G. R. R. P. R. R. on this sheet (the West Jersey and Seashore line elsewhere).
Railroad Place is marked arbitrary (a name given by the map makers).
Central Avenue is followed by NJ 73 today; Chestnut Avenue is Washington Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Skillman-Thomas coal yard, concrete block works and the railroad station.

50 ft, one part (rotation about -42). Central Av (Oak; NJ 73 today), Oak Av, Taunton Av, Chestnut Av (Washington Av today), Railroad Pl (arbitrary), Jefferson Av; station, Skillman-Thomas coal yard. Only 4 junctions, mostly along Taunton Av; a hand-picked Oak Av / Central Av point disagreed by 9 m and was removed.

sheet-7.description: Sheet 7 shows a built-up residential and commercial district on the west side of White Horse Pike in Berlin, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right. Four streets cross the sheet from left to right, Thackery Avenue at the top, then Rich Avenue, Broad and Estaugh Avenue, and two run down the page, Moss Avenue near the left edge and Central Avenue in the middle; White Horse Pike forms the right edge. The blocks are numbered 37, 39 and 41 on the left, 18, 20 and 21 on the right, with parts of 22 and 43 along the bottom. The left half is mostly frame dwellings with auto houses on large lots, with an Episcopal church of brick, heated by hot air and lit by electricity, on block 39, and the compass rose in the open upper left. On Central Avenue the Henry Funeral Home and an undertaker stand on block 18. The blocks facing the Pike carry the commercial buildings: the Berlin Bottling Co. with a shipping house, stores and dwellings, an auto repairing shop of cement floor, Auto Sales and Service with a showroom and stores, and the J. W. Bundy garage with a capacity of 36 cars, auto supplies and chemical extinguishers. Narrow strips of neighbouring blocks appear at the left margin, where the notation No Exposure is lettered. Four-inch water pipes run in the cross streets and hydrants stand at the corners.
notes: Thackery Avenue is Thackara Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Broad is West Broad Avenue in OpenStreetMap west of the Pike.
White Horse Pike is South White Horse Pike in OpenStreetMap along this sheet.
The junction of Thackery Avenue and the Pike was left out of the control: it lies at the sheet edge and the street was measured narrower than drawn.

50 ft, one part (rotation about +26). Thackery Av (Thackara), Rich Av, Broad (West Broad Av), Estaugh Av, Moss Av, Central Av, White Horse Pike. Mask top set at the Thackery Av centreline so its margin and cartouche do not cover sheet 9.

sheet-8.description: Sheet 8 lies east of White Horse Pike in the middle of Berlin, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right. The Pike runs down the left edge, with the ends of Rich Avenue, Broad Street and Estaugh Avenue lettered in the margin where they meet it from the west. Haines Avenue runs from Smithfield Avenue at the top down the page, bending to the right near the bottom to meet Taunton Avenue, which crosses the lower right corner. Garwood Avenue crosses at the upper right and ends at the railroad tracks of the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad (Pennsylvania Railroad), shown as a band of lines in the upper right corner. Between the Pike and Haines Avenue, blocks 9 and 19 are long narrow lots holding frame dwellings with auto houses, and along the Pike itself stand a lodge, a vulcanizing shop, a movie house of cement-block construction, the Baptist Church with its chapel, the Boro Hall, a tin shop, and the Centenary M.E. Church with its chapel, which heat by furnace and light by electricity. The First Presbyterian Church, with a tower, stands at the bottom near Taunton Avenue. East of Haines Avenue the ground is largely open: a few dwellings face the avenue on block 221 and the remaining lots, among them the large block 32, are empty. A compass rose with a north arrow stands in the open land at the right. Six-inch water pipes run in Haines, Smithfield and Taunton Avenues, with ten-inch and six-inch pipes in the Pike.
notes: White Horse Pike is South White Horse Pike in OpenStreetMap along this sheet.
Broad Street is East Broad Street in OpenStreetMap east of the Pike; it is not drawn crossing Haines Avenue, which OpenStreetMap shows as a junction.
The control points where the streets meet the Pike and at Smithfield Avenue were hand-picked.

50 ft, one part (rotation about +26.5). White Horse Pike at the left edge, Rich Av, Broad St (East Broad Street), Estaugh Av, Haines Av, Garwood Av, Smithfield Av, Taunton Av; Baptist and Centenary M.E. churches, Boro Hall, 1st Presbyterian church. 4 of 6 points hand-picked (pike junctions, Haines / Smithfield).

sheet-9.description: Sheet 9 shows the northern end of Berlin, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right. White Horse Pike runs up the middle of the sheet from Thackery Avenue at the bottom to a crossroads at the top, where Albion Road comes in from the lower left and Milford Road leaves to the right in a long curve towards the railroad. Harkers Avenue crosses east of the Pike and Haines Avenue forms the right edge; Thackery Avenue runs along the bottom, with Central Avenue at the lower left corner. The West Jersey and Seashore Railroad (Pennsylvania Railroad), a band of four tracks, crosses the upper right corner, with Reed Crossing Station, a small frame building, beside it. West of the Pike the land is largely open (block 15), with a bus garage of cement-block walls holding 15 cars, a few dwellings and a store at the lower end, and a row of lots with frame dwellings and outbuildings along Albion Road on block 195. East of the Pike, block 16 holds two hay and feed dealers' buildings, a dwelling and the Berlin Auto Body Works, and further south the Simon Fisher ladies garment factory of cement-block construction with the Shultz Mfg. Co. 2nd building beside it. The Berlin Public School, a large two-wing brick building heated by steam with a separate frame annex, stands on block 19 beside Haines Avenue. A compass rose lies in the open upper left. Large parts of blocks 218 and 19 are open land.
notes: Harkers Avenue is Harker Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Thackery Avenue is Thackara Avenue in OpenStreetMap west of the Pike; its continuation east of the Pike, unnamed on the sheet, is Smithfield Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Albion Road lies on Berlin-Cross Keys Road in OpenStreetMap.
White Horse Pike is South White Horse Pike in OpenStreetMap, which splits into South and West White Horse Pike near the top of the sheet.
The crossroads at the top (Albion Road, Milford Road and the Pike) was hand-picked at the drawn centre and lay about 7 m from the modern node, so it was left out of the control.

50 ft, one part (rotation about +27). White Horse Pike, Albion Rd (Berlin-Cross Keys Road), Milford Rd, Harkers Av (Harker), Haines Av, Thackery Av, Central Av; Berlin Public School, Simon Fisher garment factory; railroad at the upper right. Top third has no control; mask notched along the railroad at the upper right (cartouche).

sheet-10.description: Sheet 10 shows an outlying subdivision on the north side of Berlin in Berlin Township, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left. The part lies between Milford Road on the left and Harker Avenue on the right, which converge towards the bottom of the sheet where the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad crosses the lower left corner. Between them a grid of platted streets, Cambridge Avenue, Arndt Avenue, Devon Avenue, Harding Avenue, Fairfax Avenue and Wright Avenue, crossed by Philips Avenue, divides blocks 222 to 229 and 52 into hundreds of narrow numbered lots, almost all of them still empty. Building is confined to the frontages of Milford Road and Wright Avenue and to scattered dwellings and auto houses east of Harker Avenue (block 54) and west of Milford Road (blocks 219 and 196), where a western section of Fairfax Avenue runs off towards the left edge. An election booth stands on Milford Road. At the foot of the sheet, between Milford Road and the railroad, is the plant of T. B. Wright and Co., makers of medical charcoal, with a pulverizing and packing building, storage and coal yards on both sides. Six-inch water pipes run in Milford Road and Harker Avenue with four-inch pipes in Wright Avenue. The left margin carries a dash-dot line and refers to sheet 11, and the bottom to sheet 9.
notes: Cambridge, Arndt, Devon, Harding and Philips Avenues are not in OpenStreetMap; the platted subdivision was not built on this plan and NJ 73 now crosses the area.
Fairfax Avenue survives only west of Milford Road; Wright Avenue survives between Milford Road and Harker Avenue.
T. B. Wright and Co. medical charcoal works by the railroad.
Only the lower half of the sheet has control points; the upper half is extrapolated.

100 ft, one part (rotation about -14). Milford Rd, Harker Av, platted subdivision (Cambridge, Arndt, Devon, Harding, Philips, Fairfax, Wright Avs) mostly never built; T. B. Wright & Co. charcoal works. Only Fairfax/Wright junctions and a rail crossing survive; upper half extrapolated, low confidence.
